title: Reduce jitter-induced token interleaving on fanout streams
creator: Asha Patel
description: Incident summary: During a capacity surge on 2026-02-16 several hosted API streaming responses to multi-tenant fanout endpoints emitted interleaved partial token fragments and duplicate token suffixes to downstream clients. Symptoms included clipped tokens, out-of-order fragments, and frequent client disconnects for long-lived sessions. Root cause analysis found a burst of jittered socket write latencies combined with a head-of-line scheduling effect in our per-worker fanout loop which allowed fragments for different sessions to be interleaved and for the server-side transmit buffer to retransmit partial token suffixes during reconnects.
timeline: 2026-02-16 02:12 UTC: First alert - elevated error rate on streaming fanout (dashboards: streaming.fanout.errors)
2026-02-16 02:18 UTC: Ops triage - rolling restart of a subset of workers temporarily reduced errors
2026-02-16 03:05 UTC: Mitigation - enabled conservative per-connection send window to reduce retransmits (hotfix: gh/pr/RED-1591)
2026-02-16 09:00 UTC: Detailed RCA start - reproduced with a local multi-tenant fanout harness
2026-02-24 14:00 UTC: Engineering review - confirmed interaction between socket jitter, fanout loop scheduling, and fragment re-emission on reconnects
postmortem_summary: A combination of transient network jitter and an opportunistic scheduling hole in the fanout send loop allowed token fragments from separate sessions to be interleaved. When clients reconnected or retransmitted, we re-emitted partial token suffixes leading to duplicate tokens and malformed outputs. This primarily affected multi-tenant fanout paths under high concurrency and medium tail-latency conditions. No model weights or user data were exposed; impact was availability/quality for streaming sessions. We estimate ~1.6% of streams during the window experienced visible corruption.
root_causes: per-worker fanout loop processes multiple connections in a single non-preemptive slice leading to cross-connection fragment interleaving
lack of session-scoped sequence numbers/fragment checksums that would allow recipients to reassemble or discard duplicate fragments
no adaptive send pacing for connections showing tail transmit latency (jitter) causing retransmits to include partial tokens
insufficient e2e tests that simulate jittered socket writes across many concurrent fanout targets
decisions: Introduce session-sequence numbers for streamed fragments to enable deterministic reassembly and de-duplication on the client-facing protocol
Implement a per-connection soft pacing token bucket in the runtime to smooth out jitter and avoid partial-token retransmits
Add an idempotent fragment ACK/NAK handshake for reconnects for long-lived streaming sessions
Expand chaos tests to include synthetic socket jitter and high-fanout interleaving scenarios
action_items: ENG-83412-A: Add fragment sequence numbers and 16-bit CRC to streaming wire format (owner: Diego Ramos, estimate: 3) - target runtime-2.3
ENG-83412-B: Implement per-connection soft pacing (token-bucket) in fanout worker loop (owner: Linnea Chen, estimate: 5)
ENG-83412-C: Extend reconnect flow to request missing fragment ranges and enable server-side fragment replay idempotency (owner: Marcus Holt, estimate: 3)
ENG-83412-D: Add telemetry: fragment_drop_rate, fragment_dup_rate, avg_send_jitter_ms, fanout_interleave_count (owner: SRE team, estimate: 2)
ENG-83412-E: Create e2e chaos test harness that injects asymmetric write jitter across 500 concurrent fanout targets (owner: QA, estimate: 4)
ENG-83412-F: Backfill dashboards and set PagerDuty thresholds for fragment_dup_rate and fanout_interleave_count (owner: SRE, estimate: 1)
ENG-83412-G: Run a 48-hour canary with sequence numbers + pacing behind a feature flag before global rollout (owner: Diego Ramos, due: 2026-03-20)
ENG-83412-H: Update client SDKs with fragment reassembly logic and graceful deduplication (owner: SDK team, estimate: 3)
ENG-83412-I: Documentation and runbook update for streaming corruption incidents (owner: Operations, estimate: 1)
runbook_updates: Runbook: streaming_corruption.md - steps to enable feature-flagged pacing and restart fanout workers safely
Troubleshooting checklist: identify top affected routes, snapshot worker send buffers, correlate with infra tail-latency events
test_plan: Unit tests for fragment sequence and CRC validation
Integration test for reconnect-led fragment replay using simulated partial-sends
Chaos test: inject per-target write jitter and validate zero interleaving in canary runs
Compatibility test matrix for older clients that lack fragment-seq support (server falls back to legacy behavior)
notes: Client compatibility: we'll support a fallback mode where server disables fragment-seq for legacy clients, but this will emit higher CPU cost — track usage before disabling fallback
Risk: adding per-fragment CRC increases wire overhead ~8 bytes/fragment; estimate token-level cost increase <0.7% under typical workloads
Operational constraint: pacing may increase p50 tail by ~5-10ms in worst-case for heavily multiplexed workers, tradeoff accepted to avoid corruption

2026-02-25 - Marcus Holt: Hotfix reduced visible corruption by ~70% in prod but didn't eliminate duplicates on reconnects.
2026-03-01 - Asha Patel: Prioritized P0; coordinated cross-team owners. SRE to instrument metrics this week.
2026-03-04 - Diego Ramos: Draft PR for fragment seq proto open for review (see PR #1627). Will gate with feature flag.
next_steps: Merge fragment-seq PR behind a feature flag and deploy to canary cluster
Roll out per-connection soft pacing to canary and run 48h validation
Enable improved telemetry and set alerts; if metrics are stable, schedule progressive rollout across regions
Coordinate SDK teams to release reassembly logic within two release cycles
